Shiphrah and Puah
SHIF-ruh POO-uh
proper noun (person)
The two Hebrew midwives who feared God and refused Pharaoh's command to kill the male infants (Exo 1:15-21).

📖 Biblical Definition

Shiphrah and Puah were two Hebrew midwives whom Pharaoh commanded to kill every male child born to the Hebrew women, that Israel's growth might be checked. "But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive" (Exo 1:17). When Pharaoh demanded why, they answered that the Hebrew women were vigorous and delivered before the midwives came. For their courageous defiance of a murderous decree, "God dealt well with the midwives... And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses" (Exo 1:20-21) — that is, He blessed them with families of their own. Their fear of God outweighed their fear of the most powerful man on earth, and they chose to protect innocent life at great personal risk rather than obey an evil law. Shiphrah and Puah stand in the dictionary as the God-fearing midwives who would not shed innocent blood, a lasting witness that the fear of God must govern obedience to human authority, that an unjust command to destroy the innocent is not to be obeyed, and that God remembers and rewards those who protect life and defy wickedness for His sake.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Two Hebrew midwives (Exo 1:15-21) who feared God and refused Pharaoh's command to kill the male infants, saving the children alive; God dealt well with them and made them houses.

SHIPHRAH AND PUAH, proper noun. Two Hebrew midwives in Egypt (Exo 1:15).

Commanded by Pharaoh to kill every male Hebrew child at birth.

"But the midwives feared God" and saved the children alive (Exo 1:17).

Refused to shed innocent blood despite the king's decree.

Rewarded by God, who "made them houses" (Exo 1:21).

📖 Key Scripture

Exo 1:17 — "But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive."

Exo 1:20 — "Therefore God dealt well with the midwives: and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty."

Exo 1:21 — "And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that he made them houses."

Acts 5:29 — "Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Shiphrah and Puah honor the recovery of the fear of God above the fear of man and of righteous refusal to obey an unjust command, against a servility that complies with evil law and a contempt for the sanctity of life.

expand to see more

Unjust-law-obeyed correction. Some teach that the believer must always obey the civil authority, even when it commands sin. Shiphrah and Puah feared God and disobeyed a direct royal command to murder, and God commended and rewarded them. The dictionary holds that human authority is to be honored within its bounds, but a command to do evil — especially to shed innocent blood — is not to be obeyed; we ought to obey God rather than men (Acts 5:29), and the fear of God governs all lesser allegiances.

This entry faces little postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the protection of innocent life as a fear-of-God duty. The midwives risked their lives to save defenseless infants. The dictionary commends their example with abiding application: the lives of the unborn and the newborn are precious to God, and those who fear Him will protect rather than destroy them, even against the decrees of the powerful. God remembers such faithfulness, and dealt well with the midwives who would not kill.
